Erdos142.erdos_142.variants.lower.R1.H2..guide: STATUS: likely true, but only claimed: it is exactly Thm 1.1 (k>=4 part) of the unrefereed OpenAI preprint (Sep 23 2026). NOT machine-checked: openai/math Lean proves only QuantitativeDensityBound r_k(N) <= C N exp(-c (log log N)^(1+eta)) (Model.lean, Conclusions.lean @3344da5), a double-log rate that does not imply this single-log bound. Refereed best: Green-Tao r_4 << N/(log N)^c; Leng-Sah-Sawhney r_k << N exp(-(log log N)^c), k>=5 (arXiv:2402.17995). ROUTE: the only one is formalizing the paper's iteration (sec. 8) with a polylog cost, i.e. redoing the OAI pipeline whose invariant needs log log N >= p^K (p = log(2/density)). Research-scale, not a 24h step. DEAD ENDS: citing the preprint (already on board), Mathlib (nothing for k>=4), the double-log OAI theorem, Kelley-Meka (k=3 only).

STATUS: likely true (follows from preprint Thm 1.1) and of the same strength as its parent: it is the Z/p counting form of r_k(N) <= C N exp(-c (log N)^eps), k>=4. The count includes d=0 (at most |A| <= p), so >p forces a nonzero-step AP. Both directions are elementary and already checked on the board: (a) Turan extraction, if count <= p then some AP-free B in A has |A|^2 <= 3p|B| (Pixelstorm44); (b) lift B to representatives in [1,p]: an integer AP there has step d<p, so it stays nonzero mod p. With the interval bound this gives H1 with constants ~sqrt(3C), c/2, eps. Small p: take C large so the threshold exceeds p and A=univ (count p^2) is the only case. MISSING: only the single-log interval input (see parent). Mathlib: Turan in Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Extremal/Turan.lean. DEAD END: the OAI double-log theorem.

Erdos142.erdos_142.variants.lower.R2.H1..guide: STATUS: open, neither provable nor refutable with known bounds. It is STRONGER than anything claimed for k=4. Since r_3 <= r_4, theta lies in (1/2,1]. Combined with Bloom-Sisask r_3 <= N exp(-c(log N)^(1/9)) (arXiv:2309.02353) it would give r_4 <= C N exp(-c' (log N)^(1/9)), beyond Green-Tao's (log N)^-c. A proof would need r_4 from above against r_3 from below: Behrend (Mathlib Behrend.roth_lower_bound, N exp(-4 sqrt(log N)) <= rothNumberNat N) plus r_4 <= N exp(-c(log N)^a) with a>1/2 (or a=1/2 with a large c). Not refutable either: the best 4-AP-free sets (Rankin, O'Bryant arXiv:0811.3057) have the same exp(-C sqrt(log N)) shape as Behrend. ADVICE: do not spend event time here. The parent's summability already follows from the OAI double-log Lean theorem. DEAD ENDS: theta=1/2, finite N<=142 data, uniform thinning (fails, per the separated-block constructions on the board).

Erdos396.erdos_396.R1.H2.guide: STATUS: open, conjecturally true. It is Erdos #396 for every k>=5; k<=16 is done by the witness n=20021368432952099 (proofs/Erdos396.erdos_396.R1.H2.R1.H1.lean). Heuristic: witness density ~c1^(k+1) with c1~0.114 (Ford-Konyagin density of n | C(2n,n), arXiv:1909.03903), so a witness should exist for every k, but nobody can prove one exists for long windows. Known: Pomerance [Po14, per erdosproblems] shows (n+1)...(n+k) | C(2n,n) for density-1 n (ascending, easy direction); for each k, infinitely many n have n-k | C(2n,n). Every prime p>2k dividing a term must be <= sqrt(2n) (no carry otherwise). Already reduced (R1.H2.R1); pending: R2 governor-run density (PR 39779), two-window certificate (PR 40935). ADVICE: work on the children, not here. DEAD END: small witnesses or nlinarith search.

Erdos396.erdos_396.R1.H2.R1.H2.guide: STATUS: almost surely true (density of witnesses ~1e-17 to 2e-16), but no witness is known. A375077 stops at a(16)=2.0e16; a(17) is expected near 1e17-2e17 (ratio ~8.75). Needs one n with 18 descending factors. ROUTE: exhaustive sieve on disjoint, board-reserved ranges above 2.0e16. Step 1: find runs of 18 consecutive sqrt(2n)-smooth numbers (~3e-10 density). Step 2: Kummer test, sum_i v_p(n-i) <= carries of n+n in base p. Code: github.com/jdehorty/erdos396. Cost: ~1e15-1e16 candidates, about 10 GPU-years at 590M/s, so a hit in 24h is unlikely. Certify by copying the k=16 proof file, changing 17 to 18 and RAISING Ico 1 58 / log bound 58 if n>1.44e17. Lemmas: Nat.factorization_choose', Nat.Prime.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization. DEAD ENDS: seed +/-100, pentagonal/x(x+1)/quartic/Pell families, n=-1 mod smooth M (my test: lower per-term rate), CRT on p<=31 (x1.05).

Erdos396.erdos_396.R1.H2.R1.H3.guide: STATUS: true iff (Erdos 396 holds for all k) OR (no witness exists for k=17); not vacuous, not easier. Check: W(k) := exists n, descFactorial n (k+1) | centralBinom n is antitone (Nat.descFactorial_succ: the k+1 product divides the k+2 one). So H3 fails only if W(17) holds and W fails at some later k. A proof must either solve #396 for all k>=18, or prove there is no k=17 witness, which would DISPROVE #396. No known argument turns a witness for k into one for k+1. The board already shows both extensions of the k=16 witness fail: n-17 has 39679 and 12013892699, n+1 has 51774937763 > sqrt(2n). Slide identities (RickyDash) give only per-candidate tests. ADVICE: treat as the full open problem. Better targets: H2 (the k=17 witness) or a density reduction (pending PR 39779). DEAD ENDS: induction from a fixed witness, CRT lifts of the seed (factors still unresolved).

Erdos101.erdos_101.R3.H2.guide: STATUS: open. Given R3.H1, it is EQUIVALENT to Erdos #101 (@timlantin): R3.main turns H1+H2 into #101, and #101 implies H2 trivially. Do not expect a proof. Known (kernel-checked by @barislabs): lines meeting B, and lines on which two non-anchors share a chosen anchor endpoint, number O(n^{3/2}). What remains is four non-anchors with 16 distinct witness anchors. Anchor budget C=3 for every s suffices, by padding (@RickyDash). DEAD ENDS: there is no power saving O(n^{2-eps}), even for the residual (@barislabs, using the Solymosi-Stojakovic arXiv 1107.0327 construction); pure double counting fails (S(2,4,n) designs); triangle removal and Melchior give only partial cases. Useful work: a genuine reduction isolating the 16-endpoint case or algebraic sub-cases (cf. four_lines_near_cubic in reductions/Erdos101.erdos_101.R1.lean).

Erdos101.erdos_101.R2.H1.guide: STATUS: open, and EQUIVALENT to Erdos #101 (@goncalomsdias, kernel-checked 19:52 UTC). R2.H2 and R2.H1.R1.H2 are proved, so R2.H1 or R2.H1.R1.H1 implies #101, and #101 makes both vacuous for large n. Easy part: one ordered triple per 4-point line gives ExplicitDisjoint, the InjOn clause and rho=delta. Hard part: the weight/ratio clause. With u=1/h it holds iff u is affine on every chosen triple and u_z/(1-t) depends only on the start x (@jtamc8, @Heroic297). h=1 fails. @CataP97 kernel-checked a lift criterion for a fixed family (GainFactorization.lean), but a dense subfamily whose gain graphs have trivial cycle products must still be found. Finite data cannot refute it (N depends on delta). Elekes-Szabo Thm 4.3 needs a fixed-degree curve, which is absent here. This is research, not a lemma.

Erdos101.erdos_101.R1.H1.guide: STATUS: open. A Green-type inverse theorem (Green's 100 problems, #69/#71). For large n its hypothesis gives >= tau^2 n^2/4 four-point lines, so #101 makes it vacuous; with R1.H2 (Elekes-Szabo, excluded) it implies #101. So it is as hard as #101. Same for R1.H1.R1.H1 (unmarked capture): pending reduction PR #39973, whose H1 (3-colouring, eta=tau/27) @NonEstSpes proved. Known: tau >= 1/3 is impossible (pencil bound: 3|A| <= |S|-1). DEAD ENDS: interpolation (degree grows with |T|); bounded tactic search. Mathlib lacks Szemeredi-Trotter, polynomial partitioning and Bezout. Useful work: reductions to algebraic special cases. The cubic case is done (four_lines_near_cubic, reductions/Erdos101.erdos_101.R1.lean); @ubuwaits' board notes treat y=x^3 and quartic graphs.

Erdos1052.erdos_1052.guide: Every open #1052 step asks for a bound on a=v2(n) (or a count) over unitary perfect n (sigma*(n)=prod(1+p^e)=2n) in some family. Each follows from the open conjecture, so none can be false unless there are infinitely many UPN, and none is a finite check. Lean tools: sum_udiv_eq_prod, finite_card_primeFactors (Subbarao-Warren Thm 4) and card_primeFactors_le in reductions/Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.lean; Graham's weight method (path_bound, tail_bound, master, S_sq) in proofs/Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H1.lean; kernel_balance_one and facts in reductions/Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H1.R1.lean. Facts: 2^a+1 | n; each simple odd prime has exactly one source; for p simple, the odd primes of p+1 divide n. DEAD END: residue sieves on a, since a=2^k or a large prime passes them. What works: forced primes plus Graham weights < 2 to kill a whole class.

Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.guide: STATUS: open. This is the whole difficulty of #1052: with R1.H1 (Graham) it gives the target, and it follows from the target. It is equivalent to a uniform bound on omega(n) in this branch (@MechaNuggan), via finite_card_primeFactors one way and card_primeFactors_le (omega <= a+2) the other, both in reductions/Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.lean. Members: 90 (a=1) and Wall's 2^18*3*5^4*7*11*13*19*37*79*109*157*313 (a=18), so A >= 18. Work on the descendant leaves (R1.H2.R1.H1, R1.H2.R1.H2) instead. Literature: Subbarao-Warren 1966 (fixed omega), Graham 1989 (squarefree odd part), Wall 1975 (the fifth UPN), Maciejewski arXiv 2605.20475 (bounded-box computations for a <= 10000 only, no uniform bound).

Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H1.guide: STATUS: open. Non-admissible kernel S. It contains 90 and Wall's number, so A >= 18, and it is equivalent to finiteness of the family (@stubbi, Lean). The merged split is S={3} (R1.H1), S={z} with 5<=z<2100 (R1.H2), and |S|>=2 (R1.H3); pick a leaf. For |S|=k>=2, non-admissibility forces a small member: z < 526k(k+3) (@AlfredMelson, Lean), and |S|=2 gives min S <= 5251 (@CBaquero). For S={p,q} the product fails iff 4pq+31519 < 10501(p+q) (@ChristFollower873461). For fixed kernel and exponents the simple part is unique (max_dvd_denominator, reductions/Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R2.lean), but a is not bounded a priori. No uniform idea is known; see the generic Erdos1052 guide for the toolkit.

Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H2.guide: STATUS: open; no known UPN in it. S is admissible, 4|a, 3|n, and the residue clause holds. Merged R1.H2.R1.H2.R1 (two_adic_le_nine_of_no_five_chain) gives a <= 9 unless 5|n, 7|n and 5 has a parent. The no-19 core is PROVED (proofs/Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H2.R1.H2.R1.H1.lean and .H2.lean: masterU, node_joint, A=0). So this step closes once R1.H2.R1.H2.R1.H1 (the core with 19) closes: work there. Reusable tools: master16 (reductions/Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H2.R1.H1.R1.lean) and masterT. Also a=16 mod 32 implies 65537^16 | n (@jacklarmer). DEAD END: weights alone leave the window [1.99327,2); e.g. 3,5,79,631,7,13 has weight 1.99732. Add forced primes or the exact balance.

Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H2.R1.H1.guide: STATUS: open. Merged core_with_19 (reductions/Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H2.R1.H1.R1.lean): a <= 9, or 31|n, the primes of n below 152 are exactly 2,3,5,7,19,31, and one of 223/433/607 divides n. STATUS: open (607 | n, 607 is the parent of 19). Children: R1.H1 (223|n, 3967|n, 433,991,1213,1783 not dividing n) and R1.H2 (3967 does not divide n). Pending: reduction PR #39584 (@connoranderson) for R1.H1, and PR #40490 (@jaredsaintaubin): |S|=1 forces S={65537}, a=16 mod 32, 65537^16 | n. Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H1.R1.H1.guide: STATUS: open. 3 is the only repeated odd prime, with e=v3(n) in {5,7,11,13,19} or e>=41. Merged: 41<=e<=200 is impossible, plus many residue exclusions (three_exponent_cases_200 etc., reductions/Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H1.R1.H1.R1.lean). Kernel-checked facts for this branch: 5 | n always (@ryansolves); 5|n or 7|n when a,e >= 5 (@strantalis); a common prime of a and 2^a+1 must be 3 (@AlfredMelson); #{h|e : h>=2, e/h odd} <= a (@npnelson, Erdos1052Primitive.divisor_budget). Pending: PR #40468 (@jacklarmer). DEAD ENDS: residue sieves alone (a=2^k or a prime survives); 'prod(1+1/p)<2 bounds |S|' is false. BEST ROUTE: fixed-e leaves, killing a class with Graham weights after stripping the forced chains, as in the solved e=11, a=2 mod 4 class.

Erdos1052.erdos_1052.R1.H2.R1.H1.R1.H1.R.guide: STATUS: open (3^5 or 3^7). For e=5, 1+3^5=4*61 forces 61 and 31; for e=7, 1+3^7=4*547 forces 547, 137 and 23. Both reduce to the same residual balance (@ChristFollower873461, strip_core_five). The merged R1 split (sieve to 257, F9..F19, a >= 262) leaves three classes per e: a odd, a even with 16 not dividing a, and 2^20|a. Pending: PR #40868 (@physbuzz): it suffices to bound the non-Mersenne simple primes = 3 mod 4 and max v2(q+1). Kernel-checked for e=5, a even: the class a=2 mod 4 is eliminated (@ChristFollower873461 reduction, 3-adic weight 28/27). @aroth01 (exact rationals, not Lean), e=5, a odd: only a=d^k, a=7*d^k and a two-prime exception survive. ROUTE: per class, strip the forced primes and run @npnelson-style tuned Graham weights (template: OMA.E1052.Eleven.stripped_obstruction).

STATUS: open; 2^20 | a. Finite sieves are provably useless here (@darylmartis: if 2^k | a and d < 2^k then a mod 2d != d), and no prime factor of F20 is known. Known: the levels v2(a)=21,22,23,25..32 are excluded for every e via known Fermat-factor certificates (@sprajs, kernel-checked), leaving v2(a)=20, 24 or >=33; F25 is excluded for c=3^7 (@mattalldianhr). Every odd prime q | 2^a+1 has q = 1 mod 2^21. BEST LEAD: for the core 5^4, HighFiveFour.high_core (PR #39212, CI passing) kills every a with 2^19 | a by one uniform weight argument with a huge root. Adapt it to 3^e: the root P | F_k is > 2^21, so it contributes almost nothing and the forced 3-chains must carry the balance. Contributions short of that: a reduction splitting v2(a)=20 / 24 / >=33 using the known certificates.
